facts.text: I am sending multiple messages and this is part 5 of them.
On 23 August 2018, the Builder issued invoice 104 for $156,113.54.
Mrs Cappello replied to the email enclosing invoice 104 on 23 August 2018.
Mrs Cappello said that finalisation of the work was close but not complete and that she had told her husband not to pay anything until all work was completed.
Mrs Cappello’s email set out a list of work said to be incomplete.
At some stage, the plaintiffs paid $75,000 in respect of invoice 104.
The plaintiffs did not pay the balance of invoice 104.
On 10 October 2018, the Builder’s solicitors issued a notice titled “Notice of Dispute and Notice of Suspension of Works” regarding payment of invoice 104.
On 10 October 2018, the notice requested a meeting to resolve the dispute.
On 18 October 2018, the Builder’s solicitors sent a notice titled “Notice of Breach of Contract” to the plaintiffs by registered post.
The “Notice of Breach of Contract” stated that the plaintiffs were in breach of cl 15.6 of the Contract by refusing to pay the balance of invoice 104 totalling $81,113.54.
The “Notice of Breach of Contract” stated that if the plaintiffs failed to rectify the breach within ten [10] working days, the Builder may end the Contract.
On 20 November 2018, the Builder’s solicitors sent a notice titled “Notice of Termination of Contract” to the plaintiffs by registered post.
The Builder relied on a report prepared by Mr Michael Sturgess, an expert quantity surveyor.
Mr Michael Sturgess inspected the work and the invoices sent by the Builder.
Mr Michael Sturgess opined that a reasonable amount for the work done by the Builder was $555,942.66.
Mr Michael Sturgess’s opinion was more than the total of $544,743.92 paid to or claimed by the Builder.
Mr Michael Sturgess identified the scope of works by reference to documents provided and measurements taken during his inspection.
Mr Michael Sturgess costed the work using Rawlinsons Australian Construction Handbook 2018 (36th Ed, Rawlinsons Publishing).
Mr Michael Sturgess used labour rates of $90 per hour for plumbing and electrical trades.
Mr Michael Sturgess used labour rates of $70 per hour for all other trades.
The plaintiffs take issue with Mr Sturgess’s evidence because the report was prepared on a quantum meruit basis rather than a contractual claim.
The plaintiffs relied on a passage from Mann v Paterson Constructions Pty Ltd (2019) 373 ALR 1; [2019] HCA 32 at [19].
The Builder’s claim included recovery of the balance of invoice 104 and a sum of $32,814.71 for work done but not invoiced.
The Builder’s evidence issue concerned work done before termination for which it had not yet issued an invoice.
The Builder is entitled to recover the balance of invoice 104 of $81,113.54.

keyphrases: Notice of Dispute and Notice of Suspension of Works
Mann v Paterson Constructions Pty Ltd 2019 HCA 32
